keys.statement: Prefer an entrainer that forms two liquid phases with the mixture, so a decanter separates and returns it; homogeneous azeotropic distillation recirculates more azeotrope and uses more energy.

plain.title: Azeotropic distillation: prefer an entrainer that forms two liquids, so a decanter recovers it
plain.when: You choose an entrainer (an added component that breaks the azeotrope) for azeotropic distillation.
plain.do: Prefer one that forms two liquid phases with the mixture, so that a decanter separates it and returns it to the column.
plain.why: The decanter does part of the separation without heat. Homogeneous azeotropic distillation recirculates more azeotrope and uses more energy.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, set phases: "VLL" and check that the condensed overhead splits into two liquids at decanter temperature.

decisions.mechanism: Liquid-liquid splitting in a decanter does part of the separation without heat.
decisions.operation: Choose a heterogeneous entrainer with a decanter.

keys.statement: Removing water azeotropically during esterification shortens the reaction and raises conversion; a cited isoamyl acetate study reports 2.7% higher conversion than ordinary water separation.

plain.title: Esterification limited by water: remove the water azeotropically as it forms
plain.when: Water limits the conversion of an esterification.
plain.do: Couple the reaction with azeotropic water removal.
plain.why: Water leaves as it forms, so the equilibrium shifts towards the ester.
plain.check: Compare conversion with and without water removal in an equilibrium model.
plain.result: A shorter reaction and higher conversion; a study cited by Guo & Wang 2019, not read by Lab, reports 2.7% higher conversion for isoamyl acetate than ordinary water separation.

decisions.mechanism: Azeotropic removal takes water out as it forms.
decisions.operation: Couple esterification with azeotropic water removal.

keys.statement: In a cited acetic acid dehydration process, a partial condenser between the column top and the decanter stopped azeotrope building up in the column and cut energy use.

plain.title: Azeotrope building up in an azeotropic dehydration column: add a partial condenser before the decanter
plain.when: In azeotropic dehydration (of acetic acid, in a study cited by Guo & Wang 2019) the azeotrope accumulates in the column.
plain.do: Put a partial condenser between the column top and the decanter.
plain.why: Part of the overhead is condensed and handled before the decanter, so the azeotrope stops building up in the column.
plain.check: A cited result not read by Lab: compare the column profiles with and without the partial condenser in a simulation.
plain.result: Less accumulation and lower energy use.

decisions.obstacle: Azeotrope accumulating in an azeotropic dehydration column.
decisions.mechanism: Part of the overhead is condensed and handled before the decanter.
decisions.operation: Add a partial condenser ahead of the decanter.
